whatThePageStates: This page is a catalogue of the GuardDuty finding types that are specific to AWS Lambda resources (findings whose resourceType is Lambda). A short intro paragraph explains the scope and points to suppression rules and trusted IP/threat lists, followed by a 'Topics' bullet list naming seven finding types, then one H2 section per finding type. Each section carries an H3 one-line description, a 'Default severity' line, a single bullet naming the generating feature ('Lambda Network Activity Monitoring'), a prose explanation, and remediation recommendations. There is no matrix, no Yes/No column, and no statement anywhere that any finding type, Region, service, or resource type is unsupported. The only coverage assertion is existential: these seven finding types exist for Lambda.

features.statuses: 7 present / supported, 0 explicitly not-supported. Split: Backdoor:Lambda/C&CActivity.B, CryptoCurrency:Lambda/BitcoinTool.B, Trojan:Lambda/BlackholeTraffic, Trojan:Lambda/DropPoint, UnauthorizedAccess:Lambda/MaliciousIPCaller.Custom, UnauthorizedAccess:Lambda/TorClient, UnauthorizedAccess:Lambda/TorRelay = 7. The 'Topics' bullet list has 7 entries and there are 7 finding-type H2 sections (the 8th H2, 'See also', is boilerplate, not a finding). 7 bullets = 7 H2 sections = 7 finding types. Every entry is stated as available; there is no No/'isn't available'/exclusion language on this page, so not-supported is ABSENT, not stated. Nothing is Partial, so there is no tri-state.
features.scope: Two attributes qualify each row but neither is a coverage dimension. (1) Every one of the 7 findings names the same generating feature, 'Lambda Network Activity Monitoring' (7 of 7), so the feature attribute is constant and adds no split. (2) Default severity varies: High for C&CActivity.B, BitcoinTool.B, TorClient and TorRelay (4); Medium for BlackholeTraffic, DropPoint and MaliciousIPCaller.Custom (3); 4+3=7. Severity is a property of a finding, not a supported/unsupported scope. The page states no per-Region, per-plan, per-tier or per-scan-method scope at all.
features.reasoning: The enumerated thing is GuardDuty's own published list of finding-type identifiers, which is a catalogue this service publishes about itself, so findingType/catalogue is exact. The unit of claim is one finding-type identifier: each H2 heading is the full identifier string, each is unique, and the Topics list matches the sections one-to-one, so rows do not collapse and distinctTargets/collapse are omitted. The claim these rows support is 'GuardDuty Lambda Protection can generate these 7 findings' — nothing more.

shouldNotExtract: The 'Topics' bullet list is a duplicate table of contents for the same 7 sections — counting it in addition to the H2 headings double-counts to 14. The '+ **Feature: **Lambda Network Activity Monitoring' bullets (7 identical copies) are an attribute of each finding, not 7 separate features and not a second axis with 7 values. 'Default severity: High/Medium' lines are finding metadata, not coverage. The intro paragraph's links to Suppression rules and Trusted IP and threat lists are navigation. The repeated 'Remediation recommendations' prose and the repeated link to 'Remediating a potentially compromised Lambda function' (7 copies) are guidance, not enumerated items. The trailing '## See also' section about 'Skills for AI coding assistants' and the aws agent-toolkit CLI command is site boilerplate and must never be harvested — it is an 8th H2 that is not a finding type. The <a name=...> anchor tags (14 of them, one per H2 and one per H3) are markup.
coverageDimensions: REGION: nothing. The page names no Region, no Region count, and no Region availability statement; any per-Region number attributed to this page is fabricated. SERVICE: one service only, and only implicitly — AWS Lambda is the subject of all 7 findings, and Amazon GuardDuty is the producing service. The page does not enumerate services and gives no service-coverage count beyond the single implied value 'Lambda'. RESOURCE TYPE: one value, stated in the intro — findings with resourceType listed as 'Lambda'. That is a scoping statement, not an enumeration of supported resource types, so this page yields no resource-type coverage count either. The only countable dimension the page gives is finding types: 7.
trap: The single most likely misparse is double counting: harvesting both the 7 'Topics' bullets and the 7 H2 headings and reporting 14 finding types. Runners-up: (a) including the '## See also' AI-coding-assistant section as an 8th finding type, or scraping the aws agent-toolkit search-skills command line as an item; (b) reading the 7 identical '+ **Feature: **Lambda Network Activity Monitoring' bullets as a second capability axis with 7 values instead of one constant attribute; (c) treating the absence of any No/unsupported marker as evidence of a Yes/No matrix and inventing a not-supported count — nothing on this page is stated as unsupported; (d) mistaking the 7 H3 one-line descriptions for extra rows, again yielding 14; (e) attributing a Region or resource-type coverage figure to a page that enumerates neither.
